full_judgment: 9. It appears that the courts below considered the evidence of D.W. 2 Md. Azizur Rahman, who served the summons on the plaintiffs, who were defendants in Other Suit No. 5 of 1988 and noticed that the D.W. 2 has proved the service of summons on the defendant no. 18(ka)-to 18 (Uma) of the earlier other Suit No. 5 of 1988 who are the present plaintiffs. The trial court therefore came to the conclusion that the plaintiff could not prove non-service of summons on them in Other Suit No. 5 of 1988 where they were defendants. This finding of the trial court was considered by the lower appellate court who also found that the summons of Other Suit No. 5 of 1988 was duly served on the defendants, who are plaintiffs of the present suit. The lower appellate court also noticed that the plaintiffs could not produce any document in support of their acquisition of title by patta in the suit land. The lower appellate court further noticed that the plaintiffs could not produce any kabuliyat or any rent receipt to prove the alleged settlement on the basis of the alleged patta. The lower appellate court found that the plaintiffs suit is barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. This was the finding of the trial court also who found that the plaintiffs could not prove their title in the suit land by any documentary evidence. All the three courts below noticed that the plaintiffs could not prove their case of non-service of summons or fraudulent suppression of summons on defendant No. 18(ka)-18(Uma), who are the present plaintiffs-petitioners. The High Court Division has correctly noticed that it has no jurisdiction to disturb the concurrent finding of fact arrived at by both the courts below and therefore rightly refused to interfere with the concurrent finding of fact of the courts below. We do not find any illegality or infirmity in the decision of the Single Bench of the High Court Division.
